4200: from a derivative of (a way, i.e. means); furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition):--gain.
4201: of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman:--Porcius.
4202: from πορνεύω; harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry:--fornication.
4203: from πόρνη; to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry:--commit (fornication).
4204: feminine of πόρνος; a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater:--harlot, whore.
4205: from (to sell; akin to the base of πιπράσκω); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine):--fornicator, whoremonger.
4206: adverb from πρό; forwards, i.e. at a distance:--far, a great way off. See also πόῤῥωθεν.
4207: from πόῤῥω with adverbial enclitic of source; from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly:--afar off.
4208: adverb comparative of πόῤῥω; further, i.e. a greater distance:--farther.
4209: of Latin origin; the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it:--purple.
4210: from πορφύρα; purpureal, i.e. bluish red:--purple.
4211: feminine of a compound of πορφύρα and πωλέω; a female trader in purple cloth:--seller of purple.
4212: multiplicative from πόσος; how many times:--how oft(-en).
4213: from the alternate of πίνω; a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught:--drink.
4214: from an absolute (who, what) and ὅς; interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many):--how great (long, many), what.
4215: probably from a derivative of the alternate of πίνω (compare πότος); a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water:--flood, river, stream, water.
4216: from ποταμός and a derivative of φορέω; river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream:--carried away of the flood.
4217: apparently from πότε and the base of ποῦ; interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort:--what (manner of).
4218: from the base of πού and τέ; indefinite adverb, at some time, ever:--afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when.
4219: from the base of ποῦ and τέ; interrogative adverb, at what time:--+ how long, when.
4220: neuter of a comparative of the base of ποῦ; interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that:--whether.
4221: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate:--cup.
4222: from a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; to furnish drink, irrigate:--give (make) to drink, feed, water.
4223: of Latin origin; little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy:--Puteoli.
4224: from the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-bout or carousal:--banqueting.
4225: genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare πόσος); as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly:--about, a certain place.
4226: genitive case of an interrogative pronoun (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as πού used with the rising slide of inquiry); as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality:--where, whither.
4227: of Latin origin; modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian:--Pudens.
4228: a primary word; a "foot" (figuratively or literally):--foot(-stool).
4229: from πράσσω; a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material):--business, matter, thing, work.
4230: from πραγματεύομαι; a transaction, i.e. negotiation:--affair.
4231: from πρᾶγμα; to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade:--occupy.
4232: of Latin origin; the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp):--(common, judgment) hall (of judgment), palace, prætorium.
4233: from a derivative of πράσσω; a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector:--officer.
4234: from πράσσω; practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function:--deed, office, work.
4235: a form of πραΰς, used in certain parts; gentle, i.e. humble:--meek.
4236: from πρᾷος; gentleness, by implication, humility:--meekness.
4237: perhaps from (a leek, and so an onion-patch); a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement):--in ranks.
4238: a primary verb; to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from ποιέω, which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally):--commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts.
4239: apparently a primary word; mild, i.e. (by implication) humble:--meek. See also πρᾷος.
4240: from πραΰς; mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility:--meekness.
4241: apparently a primary verb; to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right):--become, comely.
4242: from πρεσβεύω; seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors):--ambassage, message.
4243: from the base of πρεσβύτερος; to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher):--be an ambassador.
4244: neuter of a presumed derivative of πρεσβύτερος; the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery":--(estate of) elder(-s), presbytery.
4245: comparative of (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter":-- elder(-est), old.
4246: from the same as πρεσβύτερος; an old man:--aged (man), old man.
4247: feminine of πρεσβύτης; an old woman:--aged woman.
4248: from πρό; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head foremost:--headlong.
4249: a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two:--saw asunder.
4250: adverb from πρό; prior, sooner:--before (that), ere.
4251: of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman:--Prisca. See also Πρίσκιλλα.
4252: diminutive of Πρίσκα; Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman:--Priscilla.
4253: a primary preposition; "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to:--above, ago, before, or ever. In the comparative, it retains the same significations.
4254: from πρό and ἄγω; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)):--bring (forth, out), go before.
4255: from πρό and αἱρέομαι; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend):--purpose.
4256: from πρό and a derivative of αἰτία; to accuse already, i.e. previously charge:--prove before.
4257: from πρό and ἀκούω; to hear already,i.e. anticipate:--hear before.
4258: from πρό and ἁμαρτάνω; to sin previously (to conversion):--sin already, heretofore sin.
4259: neuter of a presumed compound of πρό and αὐλή; a forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way):--porch.
4260: from πρό and the base of βάσις; to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years):--+ be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.
4261: from πρό and βάλλω; to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate:--put forward, shoot forth.
4262: from πρόβατον; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem:--sheep (market).
4263: probably neuter of a presumed derivative of προβαίνω; something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively):--sheep(-fold).
4264: from πρό and a reduplicated form of βιάζω; to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate:--draw, before instruct.
4265: from πρό and βλέπω; to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance:--provide.
4266: from πρό and γίνομαι; to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired:--be past.
4267: from πρό and γινώσκω; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee:--foreknow (ordain), know (before).
4270: from πρό and γράφω; to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe:--before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).
4271: from πρό and δῆλος; plain before all men, i.e. obvious:--evident, manifest (open) beforehand.
4272: from πρό and δίδωμι; to give before the other party has given:--first give.
4273: from προδίδωμι (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); a surrender:--betrayer, traitor.
4274: from the alternate of προτρέχω; a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor):--forerunner.
4275: from πρό and εἴδω; foresee:--foresee, saw before.
4276: from πρό and ἐλπίζω; to hope in advance of other confirmation:--first trust.
4277: from πρό and ἔπω; to say already, to predict:--forewarn, say (speak, tell) before. Compare προερέω.
4278: from πρό and ἐνάρχομαι; to commence already:--begin (before).
4279: middle voice from πρό and ἐπαγγέλλω; to promise of old:--promise before.
4280: from πρό and ἐρέω; used as alternate of προέπω; to say already, predict:--foretell, say (speak, tell) before.
4281: from πρό and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time):--go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.
4282: from πρό and ἑτοιμάζω; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively):--ordain before, prepare afore.
4283: middle voice from πρό and εὐαγγελίζω; to announce glad news in advance:--preach before the gospel.
4284: middle voice from πρό and ἔχω; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel:--be better.
4285: from πρό and ἡγέομαι; to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference:--prefer.
4286: from προτίθεμαι; a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God:--purpose, shew(-bread).
4287: from πρό and a derivative of τίθημι; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with ἡμέρα implied) a designated day:--time appointed.
4288: from πρόθυμος; predisposition, i.e. alacrity:--forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.
4289: from πρό and θυμός; forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity:--ready, willing.
4291: from πρό and ἵστημι; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise:--maintain, be over, rule.
4292: middle voice from πρό and καλέω; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate:--provoke.
4293: from πρό and καταγγέλλω; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise:--foretell, have notice, (shew) before.
4294: from πρό and καταρτίζω; to prepare in advance:--make up beforehand.
4295: from πρό and κεῖμαι; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward):--be first, set before (forth).
4296: from πρό and κηρύσσω; to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance:--before (first) preach.
4297: from προκόπτω; progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively):--furtherance, profit.
4298: from πρό and κόπτω; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along):--increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.
4299: from a compound of πρό and κρίνω; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession:--prefer one before another.
